newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Edelnor joins natgas pipeline project.
newsitem.headline: Chile Edelnor joins natgas pipeline project.

text.p: Chilean electricity generator Edelnor has joined the Norgas natural gas pipeline project planned by Chile's Electroandina and Argentine firm Techint, said Electroandina general manager Joss Remacle.
"Edelnor is putting out a press release in which they say that they are entering the Norgas scheme in equal conditions as us and Techint," Remacle told reporters at an energy seminar.
The Norgas consortium will have three equal partners, each with a 33 percent stake, he said.
Chilgener is building power plants at Salta in northern Argentina and will bring electricity to Chile using a transmission line across the Andes.
Remacle said firms in discussions with Norgas may include Canadian energy company NOVA Corp, currently Chilgener's partner in the GasAndes scheme in central Chile.
Electroandina, owned by a Chilean/Spanish/Belgian group, will use gas transported by Norgas to fuel two combined cycle power units it will build at its Tocopilla power plant.
Edelnor, which is 65 percent owned by Southern Electric , will also use the gas for electricity generation.
Remacle said Norgas received inquiries this week from three more firms interested in using the consortium to transport natural gas, said Remacle.
If all these contracts materialize, then Norgas will have guaranteed demand for five million cubic meters of gas a day which is above the minimum level required to go ahead with the plan, he said.
Friday is closing date for offers from customers interested in signing up gas deals with the group.
